title: Workspace Models: Lightweight Robotic Memory via Saliency-Driven Supervision
why_read: A robotics memory technique that distills expensive vision-language model reasoning into a lightweight token usable cheaply at deployment time.
analysis: This paper addresses the problem that long-horizon robot manipulation tasks require memory of past events, but feeding a robot's full history into a policy causes it to latch onto spurious correlations and hurts performance. Existing fixes call a vision-language model repeatedly during actual robot operation to compress history, which is computationally expensive. The authors instead train a compact 'workspace token' offline using VLM supervision, then use only this lightweight token at deployment, removing the need for costly VLM calls while apparently also improving task performance. It's a solid, narrow contribution to efficient robot policy architectures rather than a broad breakthrough.
